definitions.explanation: Firmly held, secured, or established. Used for things that are reliably solid, like a firm handshake, solid defense, or secure promise.

definitions.gloss: strict; upright; serious; rigid in character
definitions.explanation: Describes a person or behavior that is strict, serious, principled, or inflexible. Can be positive (reliable, upright) or negative (stiff, uptight).

examples.japanese: {堅|かた}い{握手|あくしゅ}を{交|か}わした。
{堅|かた}い{守|まも}りで{失点|しってん}を{防|ふせ}いだ。
examples.english: A solid defense prevented them from scoring.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{当選|とうせん}は{堅|かた}いと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: His election victory is said to be a sure thing.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{堅|かた}い{人|ひと}だ。
そんなに{堅|かた}いことを{言|い}うなよ。
examples.english: Don't be so rigid about it.

examples.japanese: {口|くち}が{堅|かた}いから{秘密|ひみつ}を{話|はな}しても{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}だよ。
examples.english: He can keep a secret, so it's fine to tell him.

notes: One of three homophones all read かたい: {固|かた}い (physically hard/solid, like frozen food), {硬|かた}い (hard in texture/stiff, like a hard mattress), and {堅|かた}い (firm/reliable/strict, abstract qualities). {堅|かた}い focuses on firmness of character, reliability, and certainty. Key collocations: {口|くち}が{堅|かた}い (tight-lipped, able to keep secrets), {堅|かた}い{商売|しょうばい} (a safe/reliable business), {頭|あたま}が{堅|かた}い (rigid/inflexible thinking), {堅|かた}い{守|まも}り (solid defense). The expression {堅|かた}いことを{言|い}う means 'to be strict/fussy about things.'
